result:
Post revisions are in place. `bun run typecheck` passes, and `bun test` passes all 6 tests, including 4 new ones that cover the whole contract.

**Behaviour:**
- **Edits keep the old version.** Each successful save stores the post's previous title, excerpt and body as a revision. Creating a post keeps nothing, and neither does a save that's rejected for invalid input or because the user isn't allowed.
- **Revisions page.** `/posts/:id/revisions` lists a post's revisions newest first, each with its title and when it was kept. The post page now shows a **History** link to it next to Edit and Delete, only for the author.
- **Restore.** Restoring puts the chosen revision back on the post and redirects to `/posts/:id`. The version it replaces is kept as a new revision, and the restored one stays in the list, so the worked example gives `Third, Second, First`.
- **Access.** Another signed-in user gets 403 on both routes, and a guest is sent to `/login`, the same as editing. A revision from a different post gets 404, even when the same author owns both posts.
- **Delete.** Deleting a post removes its revisions and leaves other posts' revisions alone. The code deletes them itself because SQLite only honours the foreign key's cascade when foreign keys are switched on.

Saving the revision and updating the post happen in one transaction, so a failed save can't leave a stray revision behind.

The tests prime CSRF tokens before each request that changes data (edit, restore, delete). Without that, those requests got a 403 from the CSRF check before reaching the new code, which would have hidden the real result.

I added a `post_revisions` table (`id`, `post_id`, `title`, `excerpt`, `body`, `created_at` as ISO text) to `db/schema.ts`, with a generated migration in `db/migrations/20260925014354_foamy_thor_girl/`, and a `PostRevision` model in `app/Models/PostRevision.ts`. `app/Http/Controllers/PostController.ts` gained a `saveWithRevision` helper used by both `update` and the new `restoreRevision` action, plus a `revisions` action, and `destroy` now deletes the post's revisions too. Both new actions reuse the policy's `update` check, which is what makes the history author-only. I added a `PostRevisionParamSchema` in `app/Http/Validators/PostValidator.ts`, the two new routes in `routes/web.ts`, and a new page `resources/js/pages/posts/Revisions.tsx`. I put the History link in `Show.tsx`, re-ran codegen to update `.guren/*.gen.ts`, and wrote the tests in `tests/PostRevisions.test.ts`.
